sets.purpose: Acts as a gentle, low-impact mechanical pump to clear fluid from the L4-L5 joint and reduce lumbar muscle fatigue from sustained sitting.

exercises.name: Slow Standing March
exercises.coachingCue: Lift your knees just high enough to engage your hips, but not so high that your lower back rounds. This acts as a gentle, low-impact mechanical pump to clear fluid from the L4-L5 joint.
exercises.warning: Do not let lower back round.

exercises.name: Calf Raises
exercises.coachingCue: Hold your desk for balance. Push straight up onto your toes.

exercises.name: Glute Squeezes
exercises.coachingCue: Stand tall and consciously squeeze your glutes. This temporarily relieves the lower back muscles from having to stabilize your pelvis.

exercises.name: Standing Wall Calf Stretch
exercises.coachingCue: Place hands flat on a wall. Step one foot back, keeping that back leg perfectly straight with the heel pressed into the floor. Keep your spine in a rigid, straight line.
exercises.warning: Keep spine in a straight rigid line.

exercises.name: Standing Quad Stretch
exercises.coachingCue: Bend one knee to bring your heel toward your glute. Keep your knees close together and your torso upright. Do not lean forward.
exercises.warning: Torso upright; do not lean forward.

exercises.name: Standing Hip Flexor Stretch
exercises.coachingCue: Step one foot back slightly into a mini-lunge. Crucial: You must brace your stomach muscles tightly. If your stomach sags, your lower back will arch and pinch the disc tear.
exercises.warning: CRUCIAL: Brace your core tightly so lower back does not arch.

exercises.name: Standing Ankle Circles
exercises.coachingCue: Stand completely upright while holding your desk for balance. Keep the spine fully decompressed while getting the blood flowing.
exercises.warning: Stand fully upright with decompressed spine.

sets.purpose: Reverses forward-head, rounded-shoulder posture from sitting. Realigns the cervical spine and relieves upper back & brachial plexus tension.

exercises.name: Standing Chin Tucks
exercises.coachingCue: Stand perfectly tall. Pull your chin straight back horizontally (like making a double chin) to align your cervical spine and release the front throat muscles.
exercises.warning: Pull straight back horizontally, do not tilt down.

exercises.name: Exaggerated Backward Shoulder Rolls
exercises.coachingCue: Shrug your shoulders straight up to your ears, roll them as far back as they will go, and pull them firmly down to un-pinch the brachial plexus nerves.
exercises.warning: Roll all the way back and pull firmly down.

exercises.name: Standing Shoulder Blade Squeezes
exercises.coachingCue: Pull your shoulder blades together as if trying to hold a pencil between them.

exercises.name: Standing Upper Trap Stretch
exercises.coachingCue: Gently tilt your left ear toward your left shoulder until you feel a stretch on the right side of your neck. Repeat on the other side.

exercises.name: Doorway Chest Opener
exercises.coachingCue: Place one forearm on a doorframe with the elbow bent at 90 degrees. Gently turn your chest away from the doorframe. Keep your abdominal muscles tight so your lower back does not arch.
exercises.warning: Keep abdominal muscles tight so lower back does not arch.

exercises.name: Vertical Overhead Reach
exercises.coachingCue: Interlock your fingers and reach both hands straight up toward the ceiling. Elongate your entire body vertically. Push strictly upward; do not lean backward.
exercises.warning: Push strictly upward; do not lean backward.

exercises.name: Wall Angels
exercises.coachingCue: Stand with your back against a wall and slide your arms up and down like making a snow angel. Keep a natural, relaxed stance—do not forcefully flatten your lower back against the wall, but do not let it aggressively arch away from it either.
exercises.warning: Natural relaxed spine, do not forcefully flatten or arch.
